nodes.notes: PROBLEM: Simplified Swin block fp16. Input (1,720,1280,32). window=4x4 (N=16), heads=1, dim=32, mlp_ratio=4 (hidden=128). Pipeline: LN1->QKV linear->scaled attn with rpe_bias->softmax->@V->proj->residual; LN2->fc1->GELU->fc2->residual. ANALYSIS: (1) Classification: mixed attention+MLP, fp16, small per-window dims, dense. (2) Reductions: LN (mean/var over C=32), softmax over N=16, dot products. (3) Layout: NHWC, contiguous. Window partition is a reshape/permute - can be folded into index arithmetic. (4) Regimes: A) attention path bandwidth-bound (small matmuls); B) MLP path bandwidth-bound (hidden=128 small); C) full fusion compute-bound on softmax/exp. (5) Knobs: tile size in tokens, fuse LN with next op, keep weights in shared mem, online softmax. (6) Skeleton: Kernel1 fused attention block per window (4x4=16 tokens) producing residual-added output; Kernel2 fused MLP block per row tile producing final residual-added output. Weights small enough to live in shared mem broadcast. (7) Families: (a) Two big fused kernels (attn-block, mlp-block) - top candidate since per-window state tiny. (b) Three kernels (LN+QKV, attn-core+proj+res, LN+MLP+res). (c) Single megakernel covering both blocks per spatial tile - risky due to residual dependency across windows aligning with MLP tiles. Choosing (a) as primary.

action.description: Write a single Triton kernel that processes one 4x4 window per program: loads 16x32 fp16 tile, applies LN1, computes QKV via tl.dot with weights staged in shared mem, computes Q@K^T + rpe_bias (16x16), softmax, @V, proj linear, adds residual, writes result. Avoids 4 separate HBM passes.
action.rationale: Per-window working set is tiny (16x32 = 1KB fp16). Fusing eliminates ~4 HBM round trips of the activation tensor (~59MB each). Tensor cores via tl.dot for QKV and proj matmuls.

kernel_summary: Simplified Swin transformer block in fp16: LayerNorm -> windowed self-attention (4x4 windows, single head, dim=32, with relative position bias) -> residual -> LayerNorm -> 2-layer MLP (hidden=128, GELU) -> residual on a (1,720,1280,32) NHWC tensor. The reference performs many small ops causing redundant HBM traffic of a ~59MB activation tensor. Per-window working set (16 tokens x 32 channels) and all weights (qkv 32x96, proj 32x32, fc1 32x128, fc2 128x32) are tiny and fit easily in shared memory, so the natural strategy is two heavily fused Triton kernels: (1) fused attention-block per window or multi-window tile, (2) fused MLP-block per token tile, both using tl.dot for tensor-core matmuls and inline LN/softmax/GELU/residual. Key constraints: tl.dot minimum tile sizes (M,N,K>=16), stable softmax over N=16, fp32 accumulation for LN/matmul, NHWC contiguous layout, must beat torch.compile baseline.
open_questions: What is torch.compile's baseline latency on RTX5090Mobile for this exact shape — does it already fuse LN+linear?
Does tl.dot achieve good utilization at M=16,K=32,N=32, or should we batch multiple windows per program?
Best BLOCK_M for the MLP kernel given hidden=128 accumulator and register budget on Blackwell SM?
Should the rpe_bias (1,1,16,16) be broadcast-loaded inside the attention kernel or pre-added into a different form?
Is LN's fp32 accumulation required for numerical match within tolerance, or is fp16 accumulation acceptable?
Should attention output be written to HBM as an intermediate, or can we further fuse it with MLP via persistent kernels across spatial tiles?
Are window count divisibilities exact (720/4=180, 1280/4=320) so we can avoid boundary masking? Yes by shape, confirm.
What is the cost of layout permutes (window partition) — can we encode them purely via index arithmetic in the kernel?
